The October 2022 status paper says the hardware 'is being built'; the July 2026 cryogenic-system paper reports 'measured performance' of the DMRadio-50L cryostat, which shows construction or commissioning well advanced by mid-2026.
intervals.quote: This experiment is being built on the Stanford University campus.

placements.note: Placement covers the DMRadio-m3 sub-experiment, which the source states is built at SLAC National Lab; DMRadio-50L is explicitly stated to be on the Stanford University campus instead (a distinct, not-yet-created site), so this single placement row does not cover the whole detector record.
placements.quote: This experiment is being built at SLAC National Lab.

summary.plain: DMRadio is a family of experiments being built at Stanford and SLAC that use a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit, instead of a microwave cavity, to search for very light dark-matter axions.
summary.technical: Lumped-element LC-resonator axion haloscopes: DMRadio-50L (1 T toroidal magnet, 5 kHz-5 MHz) on the Stanford University campus and DMRadio-m3 (4 T solenoidal magnet, 30-200 MHz) at SLAC; under construction as of the October 2022 status paper (arXiv:2210.07215); a July 2026 paper (arXiv:2607.05771) reports measured performance of the DMRadio-50L cryogenic system and refers to future data taking.

technology.note: Classified as `lumped_element_resonator`, the technology class for lumped-element LC haloscopes; the sourced `technology` free-text description is unchanged and no claim beyond it is made.
technology.value: Lumped-element resonant LC-circuit axion dark-matter search: a toroidal (DMRadio-50L) or solenoidal (DMRadio-m3) magnet coupled to a high-Q LC oscillator and SQUID readout, sensitive to sub-microwave-frequency axion-induced currents rather than a resonant cavity.
